source_type_decision.reason: Both restored source rows ask for a conceptual distinction between shallow and deep copying, with one variant emphasizing nested structures and the other testing impact. The correct response is a semantics-and-boundaries comparison rather than a single implementation recipe.

primary_sources_checked.title: Object (Java SE 25 & JDK 25): clone()
verified_claims: Object.clone() creates a new instance and initializes fields with the same contents as if by assignment; field contents are not themselves cloned, so the operation is shallow
independence may require replacing references to mutable objects in the deep structure with copies, while primitive fields or references to immutable objects usually need no such modification

primary_sources_checked.title: Cloneable (Java SE 25 & JDK 25)
verified_claims: Cloneable is a marker that permits Object.clone() to make a field-for-field copy; without it Object.clone() throws CloneNotSupportedException
Cloneable contains no clone method, and classes conventionally expose their own public clone when using this mechanism

primary_sources_checked.title: Java Language Specification SE 25, Chapter 10 Arrays
verified_claims: array types expose a public clone method returning the array type
cloning a multidimensional array is shallow: only one new array is created and the subarrays are shared

primary_sources_checked.title: ArrayList (Java SE 25 & JDK 25): clone()
verified_claims: ArrayList.clone() returns a shallow copy and the elements themselves are not copied

primary_sources_checked.title: IdentityHashMap (Java SE 25 & JDK 25)
verified_claims: IdentityHashMap uses reference equality instead of object equality for keys
the JDK documentation names topology-preserving object-graph transformations such as deep-copying as a typical use and requires a node table of already-processed object references

primary_sources_checked.title: ObjectOutputStream (Java SE 25 & JDK 25)
verified_claims: ObjectOutputStream writes serializable object graphs transitively
multiple references to one object are encoded with reference sharing so the graph can be restored to the same shape

primary_sources_checked.title: java.io package (Java SE 25 & JDK 25)
verified_claims: the Java SE 25 package documentation warns that deserialization of untrusted data is inherently dangerous

findings.finding: The candidate directly distinguishes top-level object identity from nested mutable aliasing and explicitly covers the source variant about testing impact by explaining how mutations can leak through shared children.
Object.clone(), Cloneable, ArrayList.clone(), and multidimensional-array clone are kept at their documented shallow-copy boundaries; the answer does not imply recursive copying from any of them.
The graph-copy algorithm uses reference identity and a pre-registered node table, which correctly handles both cycles and repeated references without collapsing distinct equals() objects.

Serialization is bounded as a serializable object-graph option rather than a universal solution, and the candidate keeps post-copy isolation separate from source-snapshot consistency under concurrent mutation.
